reason: 'characteristic' is the root PATO term. The examples are 'A or B' lists of different attributes (texture, shape, orientation), so the pair only comes from a wrong reading. A rule should split the lists instead.
Delicate or fragile branches are a normal description.
Root term 'characteristic' with 'A or B' lists (herbaceous or papery, simple or pinnate). The pair carries no information.
Wrinkled auricles are correctly annotated.
A convex ligule is correctly annotated.
Obovate lodicules (squamellae) are correctly annotated.
Shiny or lustrous surfaces occur on many parts (for example pseudobulbs). The examples match 'glistening'.
A large rostellum is a normal description of size.
Fimbriate margins and discs are valid. Some examples ('with 3 longitudinal fimbriate lamellae') name the sub-part, but the pair is meaningful.
Root term 'characteristic'. The examples are sexual state (male, barren, staminate, sterile), which needs a sex or fertility quality, not this term.
'Spatial pattern' is too generic. The examples are venation (reticulate) and imbrication of lobes, which are different things. They need specific terms.
'Stellate' here describes the hair type (stellate tomentose or pubescent) on the pedicel, not the shape of the pedicel. This is a wrong reading. A rule should map it to indumentum.
An emarginate orifice or apex of a utricle is valid. The pair is meaningful, though the examples name the orifice.
Hispidulous fruit surface (hairs) is a normal description.
Length with a measured value applies to any part.
A divided frond or blade (pectinately divided to the costa) is valid. A few examples are negated.
The examples count papillae borne on the cell ('apex with 4 papillae'). That is a part count of another part, not a presence quality of the papilla cell itself.
An echinate or aculeate perispore is spiny, so this fits.
Chestnut-brown bracts are correctly annotated.
A thick or thickened lamina is correctly annotated.
Flat lateral veins (not raised or sunken) are valid.
Mixed readings: reticulate venation, glandular punctation and valvate aestivation. 'Spatial pattern' is too generic for them.
Cleft peristome teeth are valid.
Slender glands are valid, but the bearer is a gland, so a gland class would be better.
Small areoles are correctly annotated.
PATO 'condensed' means something else. 'Compressed' (flattened) capsules need a flattened or compressed shape term.
A velvety (velutinous) legume is valid.
Papillose gemmae are a surface texture. The specific papillate value is better if it exists, but the attribute is fine.
Branched paraphyllia are valid in bryophytes.
Trilobed capsules are correctly annotated.
Axillary position of staminate flowers is valid.
An oblique hypanthium is valid.
Sigmoid is correct for curved structures.
Recurrent veins or veinlets are valid in fern venation.
An ovate spore capsule mouth is valid.
Long, with a measured length, applies to any part.
A bristly plant (indumentum) is a common description.
Revolute margins of lobes are valid. The quality really belongs to the margin, but the pair is meaningful.
A funnelform tube (perianth tube) is correctly annotated.
'Filiferous' means bearing threads, not being thread-like. It is a wrong reading of 'filamentous'.
'Branches few' counts the branches. The count belongs to the parent, as in the counted-parts rule, not to the branch.
A pitted receptacle is correctly annotated.
Hispidulous plant vestiture is valid.
A saccate sepal base is a pouch, which is concave. This is valid.
A cupped lamina is valid.
A long spadix is valid. 'Longer than spathe' is a comparison, which is also fine.
Prismatic fruits (cypselae) are valid.
Flattened parts, including dorsally or laterally flattened, are valid.
A cuneate base is a standard term.
An elliptic perigynium is correct.
Shoot height or length is valid.
Pale hairs mean low colour saturation. This is acceptable.
Pollen sac colour is correctly annotated.
A subcylindric involucre is correct.
Ciliate involucre margins are valid.
Length with a measured value applies to any part.
Spine colour is correctly annotated.
Pitted sides are valid, as in seeds or fruits.
'Armed with stinging hairs' describes the presence of hairs on the stem. It is not the stem's spatial disposition, so a rule should map it to indumentum or armature.
'Uniform' may mean uniform width or uniform form of the sporophylls. A rule would need the attribute named in the text (width, shape) to tell the cases apart.
